analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 26727-28099). The file is a public prompt-contract golden-vector fixture covering request_body, provider_body, template_input, plan (prompt_contract_id, block_boundaries, chain_hash) and token_ids. The visible content is synthetic ('Public synthetic cache-parity input'), with no secrets, credentials, keys, tokens or real consumer data. The patch changes shown in file_changes are data-only: an additional_context.enable_thinking=false member added to a template_input, and regenerated prompt_token_count, chain_hash and token_ids, which are consistent with a prompt-template change. No executable code, authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or routing logic changes in this file, so TB-011/TB-002/A-016 controls (final-handoff authorization, App Attest grants) are not touched.

Only the fixture side is visible. The producing and consuming Swift/Go code (prompt renderer, cache key and chain-hash derivation) is not in the supplied evidence. That code determines whether prefix-cache block hashes (T-041 cross-tenant cache and timing oracle) are scoped per tenant/scope_id, whether the new additional_context field is injected only by trusted code (not consumer-controlled), and whether the fixtures remain consistent with the provider code. These are unverified contracts, not findings. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the changed ranges elsewhere in the file (e.g. lines 3020-3926, 43739-54088) were not supplied as units, so I cannot confirm those hunks are equally benign. The chain_hash values appear to be public vectors for synthetic input, not secrets. A reviewer should confirm that cache chain hashes are keyed/HMAC-scoped in production (T-041), and that _darkbloom_prompt_date and additional_context cannot be set by consumers to alter prompts or cache partitioning.
